speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with right leg weakness, unsteady gait, falls, forgetfulness, and paranoid behavior. To understand the timeline and progression of these symptoms, can you tell me when they first started and if they are getting worse?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy (CAA) with associated dementia and potential cerebral amyloid angiopathy-related inflammation (CAAri), though vascular dementia or neurosyphilis remain in the differential. REQUEST IMAGES: Brain MRI with contrast and FLAIR sequences. REQUEST TEST: CSF analysis for amyloid beta, tau, and syphilis serology.
